metaTitle: Atmos X · Cool your neighbourhood with NASA data
metaDescription: Find the hottest blocks around you from NASA satellite data, get a cooling plan with trees, cool roofs and shade, and track every tree you plant.
eyebrow: NASA Space Apps 2026 · Dhaka and worldwide
title: Cool your neighbourhood, block by block
sub: Atmos X finds the hottest blocks around you from NASA satellite data, builds a cooling plan with trees, cool roofs and shade, and tracks every tree you plant until it's proven alive.
nasaCount: {n} NASA datasets in use right now

problem.title: The problem
problem.sub: Cities heat up unevenly. Two streets apart, one block can be several degrees hotter than the next, and the people living there often can't see why.

concrete.title: Concrete stores heat
concrete.body: Sealed ground and dark roofs soak up the sun all day. Satellites see these surfaces burning hotter than parks and water.

nights.title: Hot nights hurt most
nights.body: Buildings release the day's heat after dark, so bodies can't recover. That is when heat becomes dangerous for children and older people.

shade.title: Shade isn't shared fairly
shade.body: Blocks with few trees and little water get the least relief. Atmos X shows where a tree or a cool roof would help most.

scan.title: Scan
scan.body: Pick a spot and a radius of 200 m to 1 km. Atmos X scores every hexagon around you.

understand.title: Understand
understand.body: See the Heat Score and what drives it: surface heat, hot nights, sealed ground, little green.

plan.title: Plan
plan.body: Set a cooling goal. Get the trees that suit the place, what they cost and where to plant them.

act.title: Act
act.body: Plant, paint a roof white or put up shade. A GPS photo and automatic checks verify each action.

track.title: Track
track.body: Check in on each tree every 15 days. Points unlock when a tree passes 90 days alive.

data.title: NASA data in use
data.sub: {n} NASA datasets feed Atmos X right now. This list is read live from the app's sources, with the date of the latest data each one gave.
data.subNone: The NASA datasets behind every number in the app.
data.unavailable: The live list isn't available right now. Open the app's About page for every source.

use.landsat: Surface temperature, reflectance and albedo for each hexagon
use.modis_lst: Night heat, 20 years of history, 1 km fallback
use.ecostress: Sharper daytime heat patterns and night heat
use.power: Climate normals, recent weather and rain deficit
use.imerg: Rain in the last 72 hours (satellite estimate)

map.title: Heat map
map.body: Hexagons scored from satellite surface heat, with a live satellite layer.

plan.title: Cooling plans
plan.body: Species, costs, planting spots and the cooling each action should bring.

trees.title: My trees
trees.body: Check-ins every 15 days with growth photos, and friends who help water.

community.title: Teams and events
community.body: Plant with neighbours, join planting drives and see your area's leaderboard.

store.title: Points store
store.body: Trees that stay alive earn points to spend on partner products, and nurseries sell saplings.

farm.title: Farmer alerts
farm.body: Heat, drought, flood and lightning alerts for your crop and its growth stage.

ask.title: Ask Atmos
ask.body: Ask why your area is hot or what to plant, in your language, answered from the app's own data.

air.title: Air quality
air.body: Measured PM2.5 stations next to model forecasts, clearly labelled.

science.title: Science notes
science.scoreTitle: How the Heat Score is made
science.scoreBody: Each hexagon is compared with its own area: daytime and night-time surface heat from satellites, plus sealed ground, missing green and how many people live there.
science.fitBody: A model fitted on {n} Dhaka hexagons explains R² {r2} of the surface heat from green cover, water and sealed ground. The app uses it to show how much each driver adds.
science.fitNone: The app fits a model of green cover, water and sealed ground against surface heat for each city, to show how much each driver adds.
science.honestBody: Every number says whether it is an observation, a model, a forecast or an estimate, with its date. Cooling and CO₂ for trees are estimates, not offsets.

credit: Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 by the Atmos X team. Dhaka is our home story; the app works worldwide.
